attempts.raw_response: When the tape becomes covered with insects or loses its stickiness, peel it away carefully and replace it with a fresh strip. For persistent infestations, consider placing natural repellents like basil, mint, or lavender near common entry points, as flies tend to avoid these strong scents. Additionally, keep your kitchen surfaces spotless, store food in sealed containers, and empty your garbage regularly to eliminate the attractants that draw flies indoors in the first place. Combining these methods will significantly reduce the fly population in your home over time, creating a more comfortable and hygienic living environment for you and your family throughout the warmer months when these pests are most active.

pair.human_continuation:
To keep the odors at a minimum, bag up and discard the whole strip once you catch a single stink bug, then replace the strip.  Keep in mind that since this is not a quick death, trapped stink bugs may give off their trademark odor after being caught. Fly tape can be purchased at a hardware store. If you prefer, make a natural sticking trap by boiling a solution of equal parts water, sugar, and corn syrup. Once it’s boiled and cooled, spread it onto a piece of cardboard.
Mix 4 cups (950 mL) of hot water with 3⁄4 cup (180 mL) of mild dish soap. Use a spray bottle to spritz this solution directly onto stink bugs or on the vegetation they’ve been gathering on.
pair.prefix: Turn it on at night to attract the bugs. As they approach the trap’s bright light, they’ll get a sudden shock of electricity. The next morning, turn off the trap and shake off or vacuum away any dead bugs. Apply sticky fly tape along windowsills, doorways, cracks, vents, and any other notable entryways around your home. Check the tape every day for trapped bugs.

source_document.title: Get Rid of Stink Bugs Naturally
